displayQuote: The most rewarding things you do in life are often the ones that look like they cannot be done

meta.title: Who really said "The most rewarding things you do in life are often the ones that look like they cannot be done"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Arnold Palmer is credited, and Quote Investigator agrees he likely said it — but the earliest trace is a 1966 U.S. Steel speech quoting him, not Palmer’s own words.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'The most rewarding things you do in life are often the ones that look like they cannot be done'?
meta.ogDescription: Credited to Arnold Palmer. Earliest documented appearance: a 1966 speech by U.S. Steel’s president quoting “Arnie Palmer.” No primary source from Palmer himself.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.sourceLine: Widely credited to Palmer, and Quote Investigator concludes he probably did say it. But the earliest documented appearance is secondhand: a speech by U.S. Steel president Leslie B. Worthington, printed in The Baytown Sun on 11 August 1966, quoting “a pretty fair golfer by the name of Arnie Palmer.” No interview, book or letter in Palmer’s own words has been located for this wording.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: The Baytown Sun (Baytown, Texas), 11 August 1966, p. 8, col. 4
Leslie B. Worthington, President of U.S. Steel Corporation, in an address delivered in Houston, Texas
“a pretty fair golfer by the name of Arnie Palmer”

docMeta.dt: Primary source in Palmer’s own words

source.excerpt: As a friend of mine up in Pennsylvania — a pretty fair golfer by the name of Arnie Palmer — remarked some time ago: “The most rewarding things you do in life are often the ones that look like they cannot be done.”
trail: Quote Investigator dates the earliest known appearance to 11 August 1966, in The Baytown Sun’s printing of the full text of a speech by U.S. Steel president Leslie B. Worthington, who credited the line to Palmer.

QI’s conclusion is deliberately hedged: it “believes that Arnold Palmer did make this remark” and found “no substantive alternative ascriptions,” while noting that the earliest citation offers only indirect testimony and that “a direct excerpt from an interview with Palmer would provide superior evidence.” We mirror that hedge rather than upgrading it.
QI then tracks the line through a 1977 compilation (Lloyd Cory, Quote Unquote) and a 1988 speaker’s handbook, both crediting Palmer — the route by which it entered the quotation-book circuit.
Palmer’s Wikiquote page carries only book-sourced lines, and this is not among them.
source.excerptNote: Worthington’s 1966 address as transcribed by Quote Investigator from The Baytown Sun. Note the framing: Palmer “remarked some time ago” — this is a speaker repeating a line he had heard, which is why the attribution is credible but not confirmed.
source.rightsNote: The earliest documented publication of this wording is 1966 — well after the 1931 cutoff for the United States public domain — and no earlier printing has been found. We therefore treat it as in copyright rather than claiming a public-domain status we cannot establish.

author.name: Arnold Palmer
author.heading: About Arnold Palmer
author.metaLine: 1929–2016 · American professional golfer, 62 PGA Tour wins
author.bio: Arnold Daniel Palmer (1929–2016) was the golfer who made golf a television sport. The son of a club professional at Latrobe Country Club in western Pennsylvania, he won 62 PGA Tour titles between 1955 and 1973, including seven major championships, and drew the galleries that became known as Arnie’s Army. He was among the inaugural inductees into the World Golf Hall of Fame in 1974.

misattribution.heading: What the web gets wrong
misattribution.intro: Nobody else is seriously credited with this line. The errors here are about where it came from, and the most popular answer is chronologically impossible.

items.who: Palmer’s memoir A Life Well Played: My Stories
items.why: Quotation sites routinely attach the line to Palmer’s 2016 memoir. That book cannot be the origin: QI documents the saying in print in 1966, fifty years earlier.

items.who: “Our most rewarding deeds are the ones that look like they can’t be done”
items.why: A 14 September 1971 advertisement in The Hutchinson News of Hutchinson, Kansas — placed by John Sutton of Sutton Transmission Service — ran this reshaped version with no attribution at all, showing how quickly the wording drifted once it was loose.

misattribution.truthLine: The credit to Palmer is sound as far as anyone can show; what is not sound is the confident sourcing. Everything traces back to one 1966 speech by somebody else.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The line reached print not through golf but through heavy industry. In August 1966 Leslie B. Worthington, then president of U.S. Steel, used it to close out an address in Houston, reaching for his Pennsylvania neighbour — Palmer was a Latrobe man — as the homely authority on attempting the impossible.

That is the ordinary way a saying becomes a quotation: not published by its author, but borrowed by a speaker who needed it, then copied into a compilation, then into another. By the time it reached the 1977 and 1988 quotation books, the 1966 speech had dropped away and only the name remained.
detailsBody: Palmer is an unusually clean case for a magnet author: Quote Investigator looked and found no rival claimant, which is rare. The gap here is not a competing name but missing paperwork — fifty years of reprinting with nobody ever producing the interview, letter or book page where Palmer said it himself.
That is why this page reads “attributed” and not “verified.” The distinction is not pedantry: it is the difference between “we found where he said it” and “we found where someone said he said it.”
context.pull: A speaker repeating a line he had heard “some time ago” is the entire documentary basis for one of golf’s most-quoted sentences.

sourcesVerified.claim: Earliest known appearance is an 11 August 1966 Baytown Sun printing of Leslie B. Worthington's speech, which credits the line to Arnie Palmer; QI believes Palmer made the remark but calls the evidence indirect.
A 14 September 1971 Hutchinson News advertisement by John Sutton printed 'Our most rewarding deeds are the ones that look like they can't be done' with no attribution.

Arnold Palmer's Wikiquote page carries only book-sourced quotations and does not include this line; it gives his life dates as September 10, 1929 - September 25, 2016 and notes 62 PGA titles 1955-1973 and inaugural 1974 World Golf Hall of Fame induction.
Arnold Daniel Palmer (September 10, 1929 - September 25, 2016) was an American professional golfer.
A Life Well Played: My Stories by Arnold Palmer is a 2016 memoir (archive.org holds a scanned copy).
